sentences.text: This revision under Section 397/401 of Cr.P.C., has been filed being aggrieved by the order dated 25.05.2022 passed by learned Third Additional Sessions Judge, Shahdol whereby charges under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471/120-B of IPC have been framed against the applicant.

2. Facts in nutshell are that Kamla Prasad (Nana) of the applicant had transferred all his immovable properties admeasuring 9.12 acres including residential house in favour of present applicant vide registered will deed dated 10.02.1982.
After the death of Kamla Prasad, all the properties were mutated in favour of his daughter Smt. Saraswati Bai through Namantaran Paji dated 10.10.88.

Smt.
Saraswati Bai had sold land bearing Khasra Number 160/3 area 0.62 acres situated at village Baruka through registered sale deed dated 08.08.08 in favour of complainant Harsh Mishra.
Husband of Smt. Saraswati Bai namely Balmukund Dwivedi was witness in the sale deed.

sentences.text: The present applicant preferred an appeal challenging the Namantaran Paji dated 10.10.88 on the basis of registered will deed executed by Kamla Prasad in his favour.

The said appeal was allowed by Sub Divisional Officer vide order dated 31.07.10 and Tehsildar was directed to mutate all the properties included in the registered will deed dated 10.02.82 in favour of applicant.

4. The Police Station Kotwali Shahdol registered FIR against the applicant and other co-accused persons on the basis of report dated 25.08.12 lodged by the complainant Harsh Mishra for offences under Section 420, 467, 471, 120-B34 of IPC.
Thereafter, charge-sheet was filed on 17.09.2014.
Present applicant had also filed Civil Suit on 18.08.2015 and the same is still pending.
Learned trial Court has framed charges against the applicant vide impugned order dated 25.05.2022 punishable under Section 420, 467, 468, 471/120-B of IPC.
5. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that dispute is purely of civil nature.
None of the ingredients of sections 420, 467, 471/120-B of IPC are attracted in the present case against the applicant.
He is claiming his right over the suit land on the basis of registered will deed dated 10.02.1982 executed in his favour.
He further submits that there is no cogent evidence against the applicant in the charge-sheet.
Sale deed was executed by Smt. Saraswati Bai behind the back of applicant when he was in service away from village.
Therefore, charges framed against the applicant deserves to be quashed.
6. Learned Panel Lawyer as well as learned counsel for the objector opposed the aforesaid contention.
7. At the stage of framing of charge, the Court has to consider prima facie evidence available on record.
It cannot consider the evidence extraneously.
The evidence is not to be weighed meticulously at this stage.
A strong suspicion, if found upon the material and presumptive value supports; the Court should frame charge against the accused person.
8. At the stage of framing of the charge, the submission of the accused is to be confined to the material produced by the police.

(See State of Orissa v. Debendra Nath Padhi (2005) 1 SCC 568 :
AIR 2005 SC 359 and State of J& K v. Sudershan Chakkar (1995) 4 SCC 181 : AIR 1995 SC 1954)."
9.

sentences.text: Though the circumstances alleged in the charge- sheet are to be established during the trial by adducing the evidence, the allegations in the charge-sheet show a prima facie case against the accused- respondents 1 and 2.
The circumstances alleged by the prosecution indicate that there are sufficient grounds for proceeding against the accused.
At the time of framing the charges, only prima facie case is to be seen; whether case is beyond reasonable doubt, is not to be seen at this stage.
At the stage of framing the charge, the court has to see if there is sufficient ground for proceeding against the accused.

sentences.text: While evaluating the materials, strict standard of proof is not required; only prima facie case against the accused to be seen.
xxx xxx xxx xxx xxx

After referring to Amit Kapoor in Dinesh Tiwari v. State of UP , the Supreme Court held that for framing charge under Section 228 CrPC, the Judge is not required to record detailed reasons as to why such charge is framed.

entities.text: Dinesh Tiwari v. State of UP
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On perusal of record and hearing of parties, if the Judge is of the opinion that there is sufficient ground for presuming that the accused has committed the offence triable by the Court of Session, he shall frame the charge against the accused for such offence.

10. What is required to be seen for framing of charges is whether there is strong suspicion which may lead to the court to think that there is ground for presuming that the accused has committed an offence.

The above proposition is supported with law laid down in the cases of Union of India v.
Prafulla Kumar, (1979) 3 SCC 4; State of Maharashtra v. Som Nath Thapa, (1996) 4 SCC 659; State of Bihar v. Ramesh Singh, (1977) 4 SCC 39, Kamlendra Bahadur Mishra v. State of UP, 2021 SCC OnLine All 503; and Shakiluddin v. State, 2022 SCC OnLine Del 52.
11.

sentences.text: In this matter there are some allegations against the applicant that he used forged document which is matter of evidence.
Hence, charges under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471/120-B of IPC are properly framed in the case.
There is no illegality or perversity in the impugned order passed by the trial Court Hence, this Court is not inclined to interfere in the impugned order.
12. Accordingly, this revision is hereby dismissed.
